title: Schema-aware multi-tenant log enrichment and correlation-aliasing pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Overview:
Deliver a new ingest pipeline component that performs schema-aware validation, tenant-scoped enrichment, and correlation-id aliasing before forwarding to downstream sinks (Loki and ELK). This ticket implements the 'hot path' transform and routing logic that sits between the edge relay and existing fanout layer.

Goals:
- Accept multi-format structured logs (json, ndjson, protobuf payloads) and normalize to a canonical JSON envelope with explicit schema versioning.
- Enrich records with tenant metadata (org_id, environment, service_owner) using the tenant metadata service with caching.
- Implement correlation-id aliasing: maintain an in-memory alias_map that reconciles multiple correlation identifiers (proxy-corrid, request-id, trace-id) into a single canonical_corrid for cross-service joins. Provide write-through hook to the correlation alias store for durable mapping.
- Provide routing policies: low-latency path to Loki with label extraction, high-throughput bulk indexing to ELK with nested fields for search. Support sampling and deterministic tenant-shaped sampling to reduce cost for high-volume customers.
- Failure modes: backpressure, per-tenant rate limiting, graceful degrade to sample-only mode with diagnostic traces.

Non-goals:
- Full schema migration tooling across historical indices (follow-up ticket).
- UI changes to Console dashboards (separate PM ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end pipeline validates and emits canonical JSON with schema_version header for 99% of representative messages in our test corpus.
2) Alias_map reduces duplicate correlation fingerprints by >= 90% in the replay test (measured on 1M messages).
3) Loki sink writes with extracted labels for org_id and service (verify trace linking in dev Loki).
4) ELK sink bulk index latency < 150ms per 1000-message bulk in staging under realistic traffic.
5) Circuit-breaker engages and switches to sampling mode when per-tenant TPS > configured threshold; documented in runbook.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Chose in-memory alias_map with periodic write-through to durable Redis to keep hot-path latency < 2ms; trade-off: additional complexity for eventual consistency across replicas.
- Schema negotiation will use the most-recent schema in the tenant's schema registry with a tolerance layer: unknown fields are preserved in 'extras' to avoid data loss during rollouts.
- Prefer label extraction for Loki to keep queries cheap; complex nested JSONs will be indexed into ELK only when fields are whitelisted by tenant.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- Add ingest.metrics.{valid,invalid,enriched,alias_hits,alias_misses,backpressure_events} counters.
- Add latency histograms for transform.hotpath_ms and sink.{loki_ms,elk_bulk_ms}.
- Provide a staging dashboard (link below) that shows alias resolution ratio, per-tenant ingest TPS, and sampling events.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge transform code behind feature flag.
2) Canary with 1% of ingress traffic from a low-risk tenant. Monitor alias_hit_rate and transform latency for 48h.
3) Expand to 20% and run load test.
4) Full rollout and deprecate old enrich step.

Migration notes:
- Provide a backfill utility that reads old raw logs and runs the canonicalizer; backfill is out-of-scope for this ticket but a debt item.

Operational runbook pointers (short):
- If alias_miss_rate > 5% and errors spike, toggle the feature flag and inspect alias store replication lag.
- For sustained ELK write latency, temporarily increase ELK bulk batch size and enable slower durable write path.
